 Advertisement 'I like Seattle': Des Moines traveler welcomes new flight option
 Advertisement Updated: 7:24 AM CST Nov 13, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Todd Magel Anchor/Reporter 'I like Seattle': Des Moines traveler welcomes new flight option
 Updated: 7:24 AM CST Nov 13, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Todd Magel Anchor/Reporter DES MOINES, Iowa — Susan Swanson is excited about having another travel option out of Des Moines.
 “I like Seattle. I'm actually headed west right now, so I think that would be great. Anytime you can add some more opportunities for us, that would be wonderful,” Swanson said while at the Des Moines Airport.
 Advertisement Alaska Airlines is launching nonstop flights from Des Moines to Seattle starting June 24, becoming the seventh passenger airline to operate out of the Des Moines Airport.
 “Today, we officially would like to welcome Alaska Airlines as Des Moines' seventh passenger airline,” said Brian Mulcahy, Des Moines Airport CEO.
 The new route will depart Des Moines around 3 p.m., providing a midday travel option for central Iowa residents and opening connections to destinations such as Hawaii and countries in Asia.
 “The great news for our travelers is this has potential to get you to Maui, should you need to go to Maui that day. So, great potential opportunities. It's great for our operations and what we do here in Des Moines, having that midday turn. So this is going to be a great asset for all of central Iowa travelers,” said Sarah Hoodjer, Des Moines Airport communications manager.
 Tickets for the new route are priced at approximately $260 one-way.
 The Des Moines Airport noted that Alaska Airlines is the first new airline added in 15 years, a move that could help reduce ticket prices.
 “When Southwest came in 2012, we saw the same thing happen, that there's some downward pressure on fares in Des Moines, and it made things more affordable out of Des Moines. So hopefully it will have the same effect here with Alaska Airlines,” Mulcahy said.
 Alaska Airlines will operate a smaller jet with seating for 70 to 80 passengers. The airline will also have a gate in the new Des Moines Airport terminal , which is set to open in January.
